prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Lugh, revered Irish warrior king of the Tuatha De Danann with fiery spear.
ANATOMY: ONE dignified adult male humanlike deity, one head, TWO eyes, TWO arms and TWO legs; fully opaque dark green wool cloak over unmarked bronze armour and trousers, long windblown brown hair. No horned helmet, rays, glowing eyes or extra limbs. Both hands grip ONE long unstoppable FIERY SPEAR [lugh-c01,lugh-c05], real flames confined to spearhead and upper shaft, no body aura.
MOMENT: Drive the fiery spear diagonally toward viewer in powerful protective battle advance, lead foot strikes wet earth, cloak swings back, resolute noble eyes directly meet viewer. Fire on spearhead throws warm light onto face and metal; ordinary sparks near spear only. No struck enemies, injury or burning buildings.
POWER: Unstoppable fiery spear [lugh-c05]. Show real flame on documented weapon only; no invented landscape fire, beams or lightning unless separately selected, and no visible divine body glow.
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low angle; very low close threequarter action, spearhead large in foreground and king face upper centre, commanding presence without claiming giant size.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one dominant cold moon or source fire if documented, deep walnut shadows, strong rim light; ordinary physical dust or spray.
SURFACE: tactile skin, coarse fully opaque cloth, wet hair, wood and stone; premium painterly brushwork.
SETTING: Battle of Mag Tuired/Moytura, terrain unbuilt and rocky [lugh-c04,lugh-c09].
MOOD: imposing active encounter, never cute, calm or decorative; sacred gods depicted reverently and majestically.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, pseudoletters, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, eyes, limbs or fingers; no film, game, anime or comic designs; fully opaque clothing on humanoids; no nudity, blood or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline, floating runes or energy ribbons.

aura: Documented appearance/deed provides presence, no generic aura.
artistic_choices: Humanlike form, bronze armour and green cloak editorial; no Long Hand enlarged anatomy inferred from epithet c03. Reverent powerful protector, original design with no film/game resemblance.
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one dignified humanlike deity, two eyes/arms/hands and two braced legs, opaque green cloak/bronze armour; both hands wield one long real spear whose head/upper shaft alone burns. Powerful protective advancing stance, no burning landscape/victims, giant size or epithet-derived anatomy. Weapon dominates foreground, no letters/aura/borrowed design. All Sangar criteria pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face, both-hand, armour-medallion, spearhead and background crops. One humanlike warrior-king deity (lugh-c01) with one head, two eyes in a hard direct stare at the viewer, and long windblown brown hair. Two arms: both hands wrap ONE long spear shaft, each counted at thumb plus four fingers in a natural grip. Two legs: the front armoured boot stamps into wet earth in the foreground, and the rear leg is braced behind. Fully opaque green wool cloak over bronze plate and leather (editorial). The medallions are knotwork discs and the spearhead is a ribbed leaf blade, with no letters or runes. The spear burns with real flame from the upper shaft through the head, throwing sparks and lighting his armour (unstoppable fiery spear, c05). The fire stays on the weapon: no body aura, beams or burning landscape. He drives the spear diagonally at the camera in a lunging battle advance across a rocky, misty upland battlefield with standing stones and tiny distant war-bands under a storm moon (Battle of Mag Tuired / Moytura, c04/c09). No struck enemy or gore. The epithet Lamfada (c03) is correctly not turned into a long arm. Heroic and dangerous, and it reads at 200px. Generic Celtic armour, not a recognisable film or game design. No text.
